coverage_note_en: Forty questions across all twelve levels, matching the blueprint's Modules 12-15 mock size of 40Q (the original 20Q build predates that sizing). Level 4 (formal writing) had zero coverage in the original 20Q build despite carrying real content — all three of its items are now tested. Questions 21-40 also round out levels 3, 5, 7, 10 (previously one question each) and add a second pass to 1, 2, 8, 9 and 11, plus two cross-level which_axis comparisons.

pair: यार वो पूरी तरह असंभव है।
pair_read_as: yaar vo puurii tarah asaṁbhav hai.
questions.question_en: Both use Sanskrit-influenced words. What separates them?
questions.explanation_en: यार marks the first as casual. Both draw on the same layer, which is the clearest demonstration that the axes are independent.

questions.audience_en: A text message to a friend you see every day.
options: कृपया बताइए कि आप कहाँ जा रहे हैं।
क्या आप कहीं जा रहे हैं?
options_read_as: kripayaa bataaie ki aap kahaaṁ jaa rahe haiṁ.
kyaa aap kahiiṁ jaa rahe haiṁ?
questions.explanation_en: The others are all correct and all put distance in. The first would read as a summons.

questions.sentence: एक छोटी सी गुज़ारिश थी।
questions.read_as: ek chhoṭii sii guzaarish thii.
questions.question_en: What is the थी doing?
questions.explanation_en: Putting the asking one step into the past makes it easier to refuse — the same instinct as English "I was wondering whether".

questions.sentence: कृपया संलग्न प्रपत्र भरकर जमा करें।
questions.read_as: kripayaa saṁlagn prapatra bharkar jamaa kareṁ.
questions.question_en: Why करें rather than कीजिए?
options: It addresses whoever picks the form up, rather than one reader now
questions.explanation_en: कीजिए is aimed at you, at this moment. A form is read by everybody who ever handles it.

pair: शिकायत दर्ज कराने के लिए यहाँ संपर्क करें।
कोई प्रॉब्लम हो तो यहाँ बता दो।
pair_read_as: shikaayat darj karaane ke lie yahaaṁ saṁpark kareṁ.
koii prôblam ho to yahaaṁ bataa do.
questions.question_en: What kind of difference is this?
questions.explanation_en: The first is institutional and Urdu-side; the second is casual and Hinglish. Both axes have moved, which is common and is why they need separating.

questions.sentence: अधिकारियों के अनुसार जाँच जारी है।
questions.read_as: adhikaariyoṁ ke anusaar jaaṁch jaarii hai.
questions.question_en: What does के अनुसार tell you?
options: That the investigation is definitely continuing
That the report is attributing the claim rather than making it
questions.explanation_en: News never speaks in its own voice. Every claim carries a source, which is why the register is so dense with ने.

options: शहर में पानी की किल्लत है और प्रदर्शन जारी है।
सूचित किया जाता है कि शहर में पानी की किल्लत है।
शहर में पानी की किल्लत, प्रदर्शन जारी
शहर में पानी नहीं आ रहा और लोग गुस्से में हैं।
options_read_as: shahar meṁ paanii kii killat hai aur pradarshan jaarii hai.
suuchit kiyaa jaataa hai ki shahar meṁ paanii kii killat hai.
shahar meṁ paanii kii killat, pradarshan jaarii
shahar meṁ paanii nahiiṁ aa rahaa aur log gusse meṁ haiṁ.
questions.explanation_en: A headline drops the auxiliary, the conjunction and the full stop. The first is the sentence it compresses.

questions.sentence: बात हो गई, काम भी निपट गया।
questions.read_as: baat ho gaii, kaam bhii nipaṭ gayaa.
questions.question_en: What makes this spoken rather than written?
options: Two compound verbs in nine words
questions.explanation_en: Vectors are dense in speech and thin in formal writing. Their number is a register signal on its own.

questions.question_en: Which word does the same job on the Sanskrit-influenced side?
questions.explanation_en: परीक्षा — and it is one of the -आ nouns that are feminine despite the ending.

questions.sentence: राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति का उद्देश्य स्पष्ट है।
questions.read_as: raaṣṭriiya shikṣaa niiti kaa uddeshya spaṣṭ hai.
questions.question_en: Why is the policy's own name on this side of the vocabulary?
options: Because it is a long name
Because this layer does the naming of institutions and policies
Because the other layers have no word for education
questions.explanation_en: तालीम is entirely current and will never name a ministry. The free words are interchangeable and the names are not.

questions.sentence: ज़िंदगी में ख़ुशी की कोई कमी नहीं।
questions.read_as: ziṁdagii meṁ ḳhushii kii koii kamii nahiiṁ.
questions.question_en: What do the dots under ज़ and ख़ signal?
questions.explanation_en: They mark Perso-Arabic vocabulary. Very many speakers and writers leave them off, and that is entirely normal.

questions.audience_en: Thanking a neighbour warmly for a favour.
options: आपके सहयोग के लिए हार्दिक धन्यवाद।
आपका आभार व्यक्त किया जाता है।
आपकी मेहरबानी का शुक्रिया अदा करता हूँ।
options_read_as: aapke sahyog ke lie haardik dhanyavaad.
aapkaa aabhaar vyakt kiyaa jaataa hai.
aapkii mehrbaanii kaa shukriyaa adaa kartaa huuṁ.
questions.explanation_en: The first has removed the person doing the thanking, which is the last thing a thank-you should do.

questions.sentence: शादी में सब बहुत ख़ुश थे।
questions.read_as: shaadii meṁ sab bahut ḳhush the.
questions.question_en: Why is there no English in this sentence?
options: The speaker does not know English
English is never used about weddings
Around ceremony and family the English tends to thin out — though how far varies a great deal
questions.explanation_en: The tendency is real and the line falls in different places for different speakers, cities and generations.

questions.sentence: कोई बात नहीं।
questions.read_as: koii baat nahiiṁ.
questions.question_en: What can this answer?
options: An apology, thanks, or an awkward moment
questions.explanation_en: It absorbs all three, which is why it is the most useful phrase in Hindi social life.

questions.audience_en: A host is serving you more food and you have had plenty.
questions.explanation_en: बस refuses the quantity rather than the thing, which leaves the offer and the host intact.

questions.sentence: देखते हैं, कोशिश करूँगा।
questions.read_as: dekhte haiṁ, koshish karuuṁgaa.
questions.question_en: What is this most likely to mean?
questions.explanation_en: Very often a no, with the word never said. A real yes usually brings a follow-up question about a time or a detail.

questions.audience_en: Disagreeing with a senior colleague in a meeting.
options: आपकी बात सही है, पर एक और पहलू भी है।
options_read_as: aapkii baat sahii hai, par ek aur pahluu bhii hai.
questions.explanation_en: Hindi disagreement concedes and then adds. The last would work in a written response, where there is no face across the table.

questions.sentence: जाँच के आदेश दिए गए हैं।
questions.read_as: jaaṁch ke aadesh die gae haiṁ.
questions.question_en: Why does a news report prefer this to प्रशासन ने जाँच के आदेश दिए हैं?
options: The passive lets the report state what happened without naming who ordered it
questions.explanation_en: Module 14 taught the form and this is what it is for. Removing the agent is the point rather than a side effect.

pair: मुझे नहीं लगता कि ऐसा होता है।
अरे यार, ऐसा थोड़ी होता है ना।
pair_read_as: mujhe nahiiṁ lagtaa ki aisaa hotaa hai.
are yaar, aisaa thoṛii hotaa hai naa.
questions.question_en: What kind of difference is this?
options: Situation — the particles have changed, not the layer
questions.explanation_en: अरे, यार, थोड़ी and ना carry the closeness. No word has moved to a different vocabulary layer.

questions.audience_en: Summing up, in one sentence, what this module has been about.
options: हमेशा औपचारिक भाषा का प्रयोग करें।
जितनी सरल भाषा हो, उतना अच्छा।
जहाँ जैसा माहौल हो, वहाँ वैसी ही भाषा चाहिए।
options_read_as: hameshaa aupchaarik bhaaṣaa kaa prayog kareṁ.
jitnii saral bhaaṣaa ho, utnaa acchaa.
jahaaṁ jaisaa maahaul ho, vahaaṁ vaisii hii bhaaṣaa chaahie.
questions.explanation_en: The first three each propose one setting for all occasions, and each would go wrong somewhere. Only the last leaves the choice where it belongs.

questions.sentence: विषय: छुट्टी हेतु आवेदन।
questions.read_as: viṣay: chhuṭṭii hetu aavedan.
questions.question_en: Why not छुट्टी हेतु के लिए आवेदन?
options: हेतु replaces के लिए — using both stacks two postpositions doing one job
के लिए is more formal than हेतु
questions.explanation_en: हेतु replaces के लिए. Using both stacks two postpositions doing one job.

questions.sentence: अतः आपसे निवेदन है कि अनुमति प्रदान करें।
questions.read_as: ataḥ aapse nivedan hai ki anumati pradaan kareṁ.
questions.question_en: अतः and एवं appear constantly in formal writing. What happens if you use them in conversation?
options: They land somewhere between comic and pompous — these words have no spoken life at all
questions.explanation_en: These words have no spoken life at all. In speech they land somewhere between comic and pompous.

questions.sentence: इस विषय पर विचार किया जा रहा है।
questions.read_as: is viṣay par vichaar kiyaa jaa rahaa hai.
questions.question_en: Would this passive construction work well if said in casual conversation?
options: Yes, passives are always more polite
No — in conversation it sounds evasive rather than polite
questions.explanation_en: A passive in conversation sounds evasive rather than polite. The construction's whole function is to erase who is doing the considering.

questions.sentence: ज़रा ये देख लीजिएगा।
questions.read_as: zaraa ye dekh liijiegaa.
questions.question_en: Is कीजिएगा simply a more polite version of कीजिए?
options: No — it signals less immediacy, not more politeness; wrong for something needed right now
No, it is actually less polite
questions.explanation_en: कीजिएगा for something you need done now sounds oddly unbothered. The two forms are for different urgencies, not different politeness levels.

questions.audience_en: Asking a busy colleague for a moment of their time, without pressuring them into a commitment.
options: क्या आप एक मिनट के लिए आएँगे?
क्या आप एक मिनट के लिए आ सकते हैं?
आप एक मिनट के लिए आइए।
options_read_as: kyaa aap ek minaṭ ke lie aaeṁge?
kyaa aap ek minaṭ ke lie aa sakte haiṁ?
aap ek minaṭ ke lie aaie.
questions.explanation_en: The future asks whether they intend to come, which sounds like demanding a commitment. सकना asks about ability, leaving an easy no.

questions.sentence: अनधिकृत प्रवेश वर्जित है।
questions.read_as: anadhikṛt pravesh varjit hai.
questions.question_en: Could this notice use मत आइए instead of stating the prohibition this way?
options: Yes, मत works fine on signs
No — मत addresses a person standing in front of you; a sign speaks to nobody in particular
No, मत is too polite for a warning
Yes, it would sound more official
questions.explanation_en: मत addresses a person standing in front of you. A wall is not speaking to anybody in particular, and prohibitions on signs are stated, not commanded.

questions.audience_en: Opening a personal email to a friend, letting them know you'll be out of town.
options: सूचित किया जाता है कि मैं शहर से बाहर रहूँगा।
मैं आपको बताना चाहता हूँ कि मैं शहर से बाहर रहूँगा।
इसके द्वारा सूचित किया जाता है।
options_read_as: suuchit kiyaa jaataa hai ki maiṁ shahar se baahar rahuuṁgaa.
maiṁ aapko bataanaa chaahtaa huuṁ ki maiṁ shahar se baahar rahuuṁgaa.
iske dvaaraa suuchit kiyaa jaataa hai.
questions.explanation_en: सूचित किया जाता है exists to erase the writer. In an email from one named person to another, erasing them makes no sense.

questions.sentence: खाना खा लिया?
questions.read_as: khaanaa khaa liyaa?
questions.question_en: Having just learned about vocabulary tendency, should a learner look for a fancier alternative to खाना here?
options: Yes, always upgrade vocabulary once you know the layers exist
No — most everyday words like खाना carry no register decision at all
Yes, खाना is always too casual for polite use
No, because खाना is actually Sanskrit-derived
questions.explanation_en: A learner who has just met the tendency axis starts hunting for alternatives everywhere. Most ordinary words, खाना included, simply don't carry that decision.

questions.sentence: पानी थोड़ा गरम कर देना।
questions.read_as: paanii thoṛaa garam kar denaa.
questions.question_en: To make this instruction more polite, what should actually change?
options: Swap पानी for जल (the Sanskrit-side word)
Swap गरम for a different word
Change the verb form — कर दीजिए rather than कर देना
Nothing; it is already fully polite
questions.explanation_en: To be more polite here you move along the situation axis — कर दीजिए rather than कर देना — not the vocabulary tendency axis. Swapping पानी for जल doesn't work the way learners expect.

questions.sentence: मीटिंग कैंसिल हो गई, मैसेज कर दिया है।
questions.read_as: miiṭiṁg kainsil ho gaii, message kar diyaa hai.
questions.question_en: What does this sentence actually show about the speaker's command of Hindi?
options: A gap in their Hindi vocabulary
Full command of Hindi grammar — gender, agreement, and two vectors are all applied correctly around the English nouns
That they don't know the Hindi words for these things
questions.explanation_en: The speaker applies gender, agreement and two vectors correctly. Code-switching is a vocabulary choice layered on fluent grammar, not a gap in it.

questions.audience_en: Asking a coworker, in a casual chat message, to share a file.
options: संचिका उच्चारित करके कड़ी साझा करें।
फ़ाइल अपलोड करके लिंक शेयर कर दो।
options_read_as: saṁchikaa uchchaarit karke kaṛii saajhaa kareṁ.
faail aploḍ karke liṁk sheyar kar do.
questions.explanation_en: The official Sanskrit-side terms संचिका and कड़ी are real and used in official writing, but they are not the natural choice for a working conversation between coworkers.

questions.sentence: आपका बहुत-बहुत शुक्रिया। / आपका हार्दिक धन्यवाद।
questions.read_as: aapkaa bahut-bahut shukriyaa. / aapkaa haardik dhanyavaad.
questions.question_en: Both mean 'thank you very much'. Is one of these the 'real' Hindi word and the other a substitute?
options: No — both are fully Hindi, chosen by setting, not by authenticity
questions.explanation_en: There is no version of the language underneath these that is more itself. The layers are what Hindi actually is, and both are chosen by setting.

questions.sentence: शिकायत दर्ज कराने के लिए यहाँ संपर्क करें।
questions.read_as: shikaayat darj karaane ke lie yahaaṁ sampark kareṁ.
questions.question_en: A learner assumes that once a sentence is formal, every word in it must be Sanskrit-derived. Is this assumption correct?
options: Yes, formal Hindi is always pure Sanskrit-derived vocabulary
No — situation and vocabulary tendency are independent axes; a formal sentence can still mix in Urdu-side words
Yes, that's the entire point of this module
No, formal Hindi never uses Sanskrit-derived words at all
questions.explanation_en: A learner who fuses the axes will write जुर्माना out of a notice and मेहरबानी out of a thank-you, and both moves are wrong for the same reason: the axes move independently.

questions.audience_en: Texting a close friend to ask where they're headed.
questions.explanation_en: Dropping the obvious तुम and हो is the natural casual choice. A learner who never drops anything sounds careful in a way that reads as distance.

questions.audience_en: You've just met someone for the first time and want to ask them to come here for a moment.
questions.explanation_en: आप is the safe default with a stranger. तू is not a beginner's shortcut for तुम — choosing it wrongly is the most serious register error available.

questions.sentence: विद्यालय में वार्षिक परीक्षा की तैयारी चल रही है।
questions.read_as: vidyaalay meṁ vaarṣik pariikṣaa kii taiyaarii chal rahii hai.
questions.question_en: Should a learner expect a whole Hindi sentence to sit cleanly on one side of the vocabulary tendency axis?
options: Yes, sentences are always consistently one layer
No — mixing an English word, an Urdu-side word, and an unmarked word within a single clause is completely normal
questions.explanation_en: The paired example mixes an English word, an Urdu-side word and an unmarked word in a single clause. That mixture is the normal case, not an exception.

questions.sentence: वो बहुत ईमानदार और ज़िम्मेदार इंसान हैं।
questions.read_as: vo bahut iimaandaar aur zimmedaar insaan haiṁ.
questions.question_en: What is the correct abstract noun ('responsibility') formed from ज़िम्मेदार?
questions.explanation_en: -ता is a Sanskrit-side suffix and does not attach here. The abstract noun from a -दार word takes -ी: ज़िम्मेदारी.

questions.sentence: अच्छा? फिर क्या हुआ?
questions.read_as: achchhaa? phir kyaa huaa?
questions.question_en: Here, is अच्छा being used to mean 'good'?
options: No — it's a conversational turn marker, showing you're listening and want to hear more
questions.explanation_en: A learner who takes अच्छा literally will miss most of what it is doing here, which is managing the conversation rather than describing anything.

pair: कृपया संलग्न प्रपत्र भरकर जमा करें।
pair_read_as: kripayaa saṁlagn prapatra bharkar jamaa kareṁ.
questions.question_en: Both are polite. What separates them?
options: The situation — personal courtesy toward one reader, versus an institutional instruction aimed at anybody who picks up the form
questions.explanation_en: Both stay polite, but one is addressed to a specific person in front of you and the other to whoever eventually reads a form — a situation-axis difference, not a tendency-axis one.

pair: राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति का उद्देश्य स्पष्ट है।
आपकी मेहरबानी का शुक्रिया अदा करता हूँ।
pair_read_as: raaṣṭriiya shikṣaa niiti kaa uddeshya spaṣṭ hai.
aapkii mehrbaanii kaa shukriyaa adaa kartaa huuṁ.
questions.question_en: Both are formal in tone. What separates them?
options: The vocabulary tendency — one leans Sanskrit-influenced, the other Urdu-influenced
questions.explanation_en: Both sit at a formal point on the situation axis, but one draws its formal vocabulary from the Sanskrit-influenced layer and the other from the Urdu-influenced layer.

module_assessment_complete.note_en: Module 15 now has complete assessment. Modules 13 and 14 still have none — Module 13 needs eleven checkpoints and a mock, Module 14 four and a mock.

phase_5_draw.draws_on: Module 11 vectors, recognised as a register signal
Module 13's finding that the Sanskrit side owns the naming

module_assessment_complete.topup_note_en: Questions 21-40 added to bring the mock from 20 to the spec's 40. Level 4 (formal writing) — completely untested before — is now fully covered, along with a second pass on the other under-tested levels.
